title: EFF Pioneer Awards 1997
notes: Electronic Frontier Foundation archived awards page (prize body, not in the authority registry, so secondary).

claim: On March 12, 1997, in Burlingame, CA, the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) was to honor former movie actress Hedy Lamarr with a special award for her co-invention of spread-spectrum broadcast communications technologies.

evidence.quote: Burlingame, CA - March 12, 1997 - In what the organization\'s spokesman describes as "a unique event both for EFF and for the Computers, Freedom, and Privacy conference," the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) will honor former movie actress Hedy Lamarr with a special award this evening for her co-invention of spread-spectrum broadcast communications technologies.

notes: Press release dated the day of the ceremony, worded in the future tense ('will honor ... this evening'). Snapshot is the PHP page source served by w2.eff.org; apostrophes appear backslash-escaped.

claim: EFF Staff Counsel Mike Godwin said his organization regards Lamarr's contribution to merit special recognition for Lamarr as well as for the late George Antheil, who, working with Lamarr, developed and patented what is now known as spread-spectrum broadcasting.

evidence.quote: EFF Staff Counsel Mike Godwin, who serves on the Pioneer Awards\' panel of judges and who has coordinated the Awards event for four of its six years, said his organization regards both Lamarr\'s contribution and the general public\'s "nearly absolute ignorance about it" to merit special recognition for Lamarr as well as for late George Antheil, who, working with Lamarr more than half a century ago, developed and patented what is now known as spread-spectrum broadcasting.
